gates.detail: 2555 of 8234 defective keys collapse more than one surface form = 31.0%. Worst keys [('قم', 30), ('بن', 29), ('قل', 28), ('من', 26), ('ل', 26), ('تن', 25), ('ت', 25), ('كن', 22)]. The key 'قل' merges ق-و-ل (قال, to say) with ق-ل-ل (أقل, fewer) -- two unrelated roots. PASSING THIS GATE MEANS THE DEFECT IS REAL.

{'قال': 'قل', 'يقول': 'قل', 'قل': 'قل', 'قيل': 'قل', 'قولوا': 'قل'} -- all five hollow-root forms reduce to one key, which LOOKS like correct grouping but is a collision: أقل (root ق-ل-ل) reduces to the same key. The medial radical is destroyed, so ق-و-ل and ق-ل-ل are indistinguishable.

{'رد': 'رد', 'ردوا': 'رد', 'يرتد': 'رتد', 'مردود': 'مردد', 'ردت': 'ردت'} -> 4 distinct keys for ONE root (ر-د-د). A matcher that splits a single root into several is unusable for the nested-interpretation work OQM requires, because the witnesses never meet.
{'كتاب/كتب': True, 'رسول/رسل': True, 'عالم/علماء': False, 'نبي/نبيون': False} -- some merge, some do not. Unreliability is WORSE than uniform failure, because it looks like it works.

62 normalised tokens collapse hamza-bearing and hamza-free raw forms, out of 14818 distinct tokens. Most are benign orthographic variants of ONE word -- but قري was in this class and was NOT benign, and I have audited NONE of the others. Sample: ['ابتغي', 'ابعث', 'اتبع', 'اتبعك', 'اتخذ', 'اتخذتم', 'اتل', 'اجعل', 'احكم', 'احمل', 'اخرج', 'اخرجوا', 'ادخلوا', 'ادعوا']

matching mechanism by version: {'v1/v2 designation': 'enumerated verb forms + uniform proclitic rule', 'v3 f-s-h / j-l-s': 'defective() contiguity + waṣla stem rule', 'v4 four narratives': 'defective() candidate generation + HAND adjudication', 'v6 Bayt/Tafseel': 'enumerated form sets per narrative', 'v8/v9 collective': 'enumerated bare-base and unit-form sets', 'v10 Iqra': "v4's hand-adjudicated list + hamza disambiguator", 'v11 YT169 table': 'enumerated form sets per row'}. Not one is a morphological analyser. There is no root extractor, no pattern matcher, no lexicon, no morphological model anywhere in this codebase. The screen does not know Arabic.

Where the screens OVER-generated candidates and then adjudicated EVERY candidate visibly -- v4, v9, v10, v11 -- the weakness of defective() was contained, because a human checked each form and the rejections were printed for audit. Where a rule was applied WITHOUT that adjudication it failed: v3's proclitic rule ate 27:8 بُورِكَ, and v8's bare-base test was applied outside its domain. Over-generate then adjudicate visibly is the only pattern here that survived contact with the corpus.

No, and it must not be read that way. Each specific finding rested on a hand-checked form list or a printed adjudication: ع-ب-س is three not two, كِذَّاب has two maṣdar witnesses not one, قري collides two roots, shadda was being deleted, 27:8 was wrongly rejected, أَبَابِيل is a hapax. Those stand. What is invalidated is any impression of general morphological competence. There is none.

Yes, and stating the fix is part of the audit. It needs a real morphological resource -- a root-annotated Quranic corpus such as the Quranic Arabic Corpus, or a morphological analyser. Neither is present in this container and neither has been used. Until one is, every root claim this screen makes must rest on an enumerated, hand-checked, printed form list, and should be read as exactly that and nothing more.

matching_mechanisms.v1/v2 designation: enumerated verb forms + uniform proclitic rule

headline.claim: There is NO morphological analyser anywhere in this codebase. Not in v1, not in v11. Every root match in every version was made either by an ENUMERATED SURFACE-FORM LIST that I curated by hand ayah by ayah, or by substring contiguity on a lossy consonant skeleton.
headline.consequence: The screen does not know Arabic. Where its answers have been right, they have been right because a human checked each surface form. The instrument contributed bookkeeping, not linguistics.
headline.what_it_HAS_genuinely_contributed: Arithmetic and citation discipline: catching that 3-b-s has three attestations and not two, that كِذَّاب has two maṣdar witnesses and not one, that قري collides two roots, that shadda was being deleted, that a proclitic rule ate 27:8. Every one of those is a bookkeeping catch on work done by someone who does know the language. That is a real and useful role, and it is very much smaller than 'Al-Mīzān'.

primary_verdict: 7/7 -- and every one of those gates PASSES BY CONFIRMING A DEFECT. The skepticism was justified. There is NO morphological analyser anywhere in this codebase: 31.0% of consonant-skeleton keys collapse multiple surface forms, the key قل merges ق-و-ل with ق-ل-ل, hollow roots lose their medial radical, geminate roots split into 4 keys, broken plurals merge unreliably, and 62 hamza-homograph tokens sit unaudited -- the class قري came from. The screen does not know Arabic. Where it has been right it has been right because I curated and printed every surface form by hand. Its real contribution has been bookkeeping -- arithmetic and citation discipline over work done by people who do know the language -- and that is a far smaller claim than Al-Mīzān.
